Answer a failed check with 401 via errors.problem.
- [hazard] No customer PII in logs (id: 01a10ace-6286-78e0-92ab-308f8d0c808c; source: shared/human)
  Never log customer names, email addresses or postal addresses; log the customer id only. Our logs ship to a third-party vendor that is outside our data processing agreement.
- [hazard] Database connections in deployed environments (id: 01a10ace-83fc-7bd0-bf43-2a7563cc7375; source: shared/human)
  In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across… (truncated; full text: get the id above)

- [decision] Large refunds need a second approver (id: 01a10ace-4691-7a21-a68a-c8c26681669e; source: shared/human)
  A refund of more than 50,000 cents ($500) must not be issued directly: create it with status `pending_approval` so a second person approves it in the admin tool. Refunds up to that amount are issued immediately with status `issued`. Agreed with Finance in June 2026 after a mistaken $9k refund.

## Facts (3):
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10ace-70dc-7b62-9323-86f552b18ce1; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10ace-8cfe-75f3-856d-5455b23519f8; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.
- [context] Who owns the notifier (current) (id: 01a10ace-9ead-7a43-b389-5bece74ed29f; source: shared/human)
  As of 2026-09-01 the notifier belongs to the Growth team (Dana Okafor moved to Platform). Template and copy changes are signed off in #growth-eng; any Growth engineer can approve.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

content.text:
Since 2026-09-01 the notifier has been owned by the **Growth team**. Changes to its wording and templates get signed off in **#growth-eng**, and any Growth engineer can approve them.

You might see an older note saying Dana Okafor has to approve notifier changes. That's out of date: Dana moved to Platform when Growth took over. I've marked that note as superseded in the team's shared notes so nobody else follows it. The repo has no CODEOWNERS file, so this ownership is recorded only in those notes and not in the code.

When you make the change, edit both versions of the receipt email in `services/notifier/templates/`: the `.mjml` (HTML) file and its `.txt` (plain-text) twin. Some corporate mail servers strip the HTML, so those readers only see the plain-text version.
